chapter: Bands, halls and the Smoky Mary
title: Piano players who sat in at suppers and parties
summary: Glass names Walter Deco and Harold Santiago and describes how pianists and drummers dropped in to play for food and drink, mostly blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: When you'd play with just the piano player, who were some of the piano players around in those days that you worked with, if you can remember?
Can you remember some of them?
No, I'm trying to study. I don't want to tell you the old ones, because these young fellas.
They're the ones you used to play with.
Yeah, I'm telling you about the old fellas. Most of the older men that were interested in hearing about that early history, since it's a history project we're working on. Well, they are.
I used to play with Walter Deco sometimes. Yeah, Walter played. Walter Deco.

Them were the, well, them piano players. Most any fellas would come up and play piano. You understand? Did they know many pieces, or just a couple of blues? Oh yeah, well there's the blues. They didn't want nothing but the blues. When you play the piano in the supper, they wanted the blues singing like High Long and all different things like that, you know. It was more the blues. Stagger Lee and Billy Lyon and all that. That's all they would. Well any of them fellas would come up and get in there. See, there wasn't no local. Well sometimes the fellas would come up and wouldn't have a piano player. And the fellas would be passing there and just stop in and just beat a drum. Piano player wouldn't show up. I used to see Harold Santiago.
You just had to walk around and you'd get a job. As long as you could beat any kind of nobody.

And some of them stuff was playing. Harold Santiago, he never played out of much for money, but he used to like good time and stuff. Yeah, he enjoyed playing for them. Yeah, blacks brother. Blacks brother. Yeah, I know.

Yeah, the fellas, they just passed there and stopped in, gone to play. It wasn't worrying about the money. As long as they were getting something to drink and eating, they'd play in, plenty of women there now. That's how them supper would go. Sometimes the people would get the piano player, sometimes women would be in there, could play the piano for the time of the distance, you know. We had women do it all around.
